title: A manager pass does not wake itself up again
goal: The loop's manager pass is meant to run when the queue is nearly empty, or when somebody changes what the app is for, whichever comes first. It is also running when neither is true. Today it ran twice inside half an hour with sixty nine tasks ready to claim, because a pass that restages an epic counts as the objectives having changed, and so wakes the next pass up. Every spurious pass costs a runner slot that would otherwise have built something, and files more tasks onto a queue that is already six times the size it is meant to be.
notes:
REPRODUCED 2026-09-13 07:40, in zsh, against the recorded timestamps.

The fault is in manager_due() at queue/bin/go-loop.sh:89. It compares the mtime of queue/objectives.json against the mtime of queue/manager/.last-run, and manager_pass() (line 105) touches that stamp BEFORE running the agent, at line 111. The manager has staging authority over objectives.json, so any pass that promotes or demotes an epic leaves objectives.json newer than its own stamp. From then on changed=1 and the ready count is ignored; the only gate left is the 1200s cooldown.

What happened today:
  06:08  the user's intake edits objectives.json (promotes icon-svg)   -> correct trigger
  07:10  manager pass runs, 65 ready; touches .last-run at 07:10
  07:13  that pass edits objectives.json (promotes icon-export, icon-grid)
  07:37  manager pass runs again, 69 ready                              -> SPURIOUS
queue/loop.log lines 127723 and 127936 have both, with their ready counts.

The reproduction, run as /tmp/mgrtest/t.zsh with manager_due() copied verbatim:
  touch -t 202609130710.00 .last-run; touch -t 202609130713.56 objectives.json
  manager_due 69 -> TRUE   (a pass runs with 69 ready)
and with the stamp touched after the pass instead:
  touch -t 202609130714.34 .last-run
  manager_due 69 -> false  (correct)

So touching the stamp again when the pass finishes is enough, and it keeps the real trigger working: an edit by anybody other than the pass itself still lands outside the pass's own window. Worth a second look at whether a crashed pass leaves the stamp unwritten, in which case touch both before and after.
acceptance: A manager pass that restages an epic itself does not cause another manager pass to run
A manager pass still runs promptly when a person or a task edits the objectives, and still runs when fewer than the low water mark of tasks are ready
The reproduction in the notes becomes a check that fails on today's code and passes after the fix, run in zsh because the loop is a zsh script
The two spurious passes from 2026-09-13 are replayed against the fixed check and neither fires
anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task
